gaps.sentence: I've always wanted ___ how to sail.
I look forward to ___ your suggestions at the meeting.
You should stop ___ so much coffee late at night.
gaps.explanation: stop + -ing = end the activity: stop drinking coffee.

gaps.sentence: He went on ___ even after the audience had left.
gaps.explanation: go on + -ing = continue the same activity; go on to do = do something next.

gaps.sentence: The teacher made us ___ the whole essay again.
gaps.explanation: 'Make someone do' — active 'make' takes the bare infinitive.

gaps.sentence: The teacher advised us ___ the essay twice.
gaps.explanation: advise + object + to-infinitive: advised us to check. (advise + -ing is possible without object: advise checking.)
too + adjective + to-infinitive: too young to stay.
Negative infinitive: promised not to be late — 'not' goes before 'to'.
